blocks.title: General formulas
blocks.content: In hyperbolic geometry, we have a good chance to get a concrete value of the volume function if we can transform our problem into either a suitable coordinate system or a model of the space, respectively. In this section, we give volume-integrals with respect to some important system of coordinates. In our computation we also use the parameter $k$ (used by J.Bolyai for the express the curvature of the hyperbolic space).

blocks.title: The case of dimension n
blocks.content:
The following lemma plays an important role in the $n$-dimensional case.

::: lemma
We have two $k$-dimensional affine subspaces $H_k$ and $H'_k$, respectively for which they intersection have dimension $k-1$. Assume that the points $P\in H_k$, $P'\in H'_k$ and $P''\in H_k\cap H'_k$ hold the relations $PP'\bot H'_k$ and $P'P''\bot H_k\cap H'_k$, respectively. Then the angle $$\alpha =\tan ^{-1}\frac{\tanh(PP')}{\sinh P'P''},$$ is independent from the position of $P$ in $H_k$.
:::

blocks.title: Further results on concrete volumes
blocks.content:
Here we mention some important results from the last few decades, which are calculate hyperbolic volumes. To investigate it we can see immediately that our formula on orthosceme has very simple building up. In this section the great latin letters mean the measures of the dihedral angles at the edges denoted by the corresponding small ones.

::: theorem
Opposite dihedral angles of ideal tetrahedron are equal to each other, $A+B+C=\pi$ and its volume $v$ is $$v=\Lambda (A)+\Lambda (B)+\Lambda (C),$$ where $\Lambda (x)=-\int \limits_{0}^x\ln|2\sin \zeta|{\mathrm d\zeta}$.
:::
